lenses.prompt: Does any requirement contradict another part of the document, an accepted decision record or the stated intent? Name both places.
Does every requirement come with an acceptance check that can pass or fail, so someone can tell when it is met?
Does the specification touch secrets, permissions, untrusted input or data that cannot be recovered, without a rule for how each is handled?
Could any requirement be read two ways that lead to different builds? Quote the words and give both readings.
What does the intent ask for that no requirement covers, such as an error case, a limit, a migration or an upgrade path?
Does every step come after the steps it depends on, and is every file, function or name a step uses either already present or created by an earlier step?
Does every step say how it is shown to work, with an exact command and the result to expect, before the next step starts?
Does any step weaken a check, widen a permission, turn off the secret guard, or put a secret in a file or on a command line?
Does every requirement of the specification or intent the plan follows map to a step, and does any step build something nothing asks for?
Can every step be carried out without guessing, or does one leave a placeholder, a vague instruction such as "handle the errors", or a back-reference such as "like the previous step"?
Is every statement about commands, options, paths, outputs and behaviour true of the code in this repository? Quote the statement and the code that disagrees.
Does every link, anchor, file and command the change refers to exist?

Does the change publish a secret, a credential or a private address, tell readers to weaken a security setting, or change what an agent instruction, skill or harness file (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, SKILL.md, or a document under docs/agents/ or docs/sdlc/) lets an agent do?
Can the intended reader follow it without reading the code, with each term of art explained on first use and each procedure in the order it is done?
Does another document in the repository now say something different about the same thing?
What does the change actually do, not what its title says, and does anything change for existing users or data, such as a rename, a removal, a format change or a migration?
Is each new or changed behaviour covered by a test, and was any existing test changed to pass: legitimately, because the correct answer changed, or by weakening a check?

Does the change add a secret or credential, a new dependency, a widened workflow permission, a disabled check, an edit to an agent or editor control file, or user input that reaches a shell, a query, a file path or a page unescaped?
What depends on the changed code, what happens when it gets bad input or a dependency fails, and is anything irreversible, such as a deletion, a data rewrite or a one-way migration?
